settings.hardware.decode: Also use the GPU for decoding
settings.hardware.decodeMore: Decodes the video on the GPU instead of the CPU. The frames then have to go back to memory for logo, lower third and slate – which is why the CPU is often faster on small chips. “Automatic” only uses the GPU if it was clearly faster than real time in the test. If the picture stutters, choose “Off”.

settings.hardware.encodeMore: With “Fully normalize” the finished picture is encoded again – the most demanding step. “Off” leaves the GPU out entirely.

settings.trailers.feedsHint: One address per line, at most 8. Leave empty for no news slates.
settings.trailers.infoHint: More pages for longer “Stay tuned” slates – on Jellyfin and Emby also slates of their own in the breaks.
settings.trailers.infoMore: From 20 seconds on, the “Stay tuned” slate turns a page every 8 seconds: the title, what it is about, the weather, the news – and fades to black at the end. On Jellyfin and Emby, weather and news also play as slates of their own on channels whose fillers are trailers from “Cinema & streaming” or “Both”. The weather comes from Open-Meteo (for Germany from the weather model of the Deutscher Wetterdienst) and is fetched every hour, the news every 15 minutes. Only headlines with source and time are shown.
settings.trailers.intro: Trailers play in breaks and as programme previews when a channel uses them as filler.
settings.trailers.listsHint: Good choices: “Upcoming blockbusters”, “Coming soon”, “Most anticipated movies”.
settings.trailers.listsMore: Plex delivers the lists in English; each title's trailer is looked for in your language – about half have one. Fetched every 12 hours; titles disappear 14 days after they dropped out of the lists. Plex streams the trailers on demand; only titles and links are stored.
settings.trailers.placeHint: One place for the whole instance. Leave empty for no weather slates.
settings.trailers.regionHint: Country code for release dates and ratings, e.g. US, GB, DE.
settings.trailers.slates: “Coming soon” slates for movies and shows
settings.trailers.slatesHint: Slates with release date, poster and plot for movies coming to theaters soon, new shows and new seasons of your shows – used as fillers like trailers.
settings.trailers.slatesMore: The data comes from The Movie Database (TMDb). Refreshed every 12 hours; titles already in your library or already released are skipped. Shows: the most popular ones starting within three months that have a description in your language. New seasons: for each of your shows with a TMDb id whose next season starts within three months (one request per show). Only titles, texts and image addresses are stored.
